title: Mechanism-Level Chemical Reaction Simulation with Electron Bookkeeping Transformer
claim: Representing every electron as a token lets a model predict moves step by step, so conservation holds by construction.
layout: 3 panels: (a) top-left, (b) top-right, (c) bottom; chemical structures, flow left-to-right
description: The figure has three panels. Panel (a), top left, shows a SMILES string being tokenized. A chlorobenzoic acid structure, with its atoms labeled, sits beside a gray box of atom-structure tokens (Cl1, C2, C3, O7, H12 and so on). Below those tokens is a gray 'Electron bag' of blue oval tokens: bonding electrons as (i,j) pairs and lone-pair electrons as (i,i) pairs. Panel (b), top right, shows the transformer architecture. A source electron (9,10) is embedded and combined with a column of color-coded atom embeddings through two matmul and softmax steps. Two bar charts give the first and second destination atom indices, and the result is the moved electron (10,11). Panel (c), bottom, shows an electrophilic aromatic substitution as two steps, τ1 and τ2. Each step has molecule drawings with curved arrow-pushing arrows, and electron-pair rewrites such as (20,33)→(20,20) sit under the long arrows. Green, red and blue accents mark atoms and tokens.
caption: Electron bookkeeping formulation for mechanism-level reaction simulation. (a) Bookkeeper converts an atom-mapped molecular state in SMILES format into an atom structure and an electron bag. (b) Given the current electron bag, Bookkeeper predicts an electron movement in stages through a transformer architecture by selecting a source electron and then predicting the first and second atom indices of the destination location. (c) Example mechanistic steps in a reaction pathway for an electrophilic aromatic substitution reaction.
abstract: Modeling chemical reaction mechanisms is central to understanding and predicting chemical reactivity. We present Electron Bookkeeping Transformer (Bookkeeper), a data-driven model that simulates chemical reactions at mechanistic resolution by generating electron movement trajectories. Following the symbolic arrow-pushing formalism in chemistry, Bookkeeper explicitly models each electron as a token and predicts its movement sequentially, ensuring mass and charge conservation during both elementary step and reaction pathway predictions by construction. On reaction-size-balanced test sets, Bookkeeper improves top-1 elementary-step accuracy, top-1 pathway rank accuracy, and top-1 to top-5 product prediction accuracy over FlowER. On the entire test set, it achieves higher elementary-step top-1 accuracy but lower pathway accuracy than FlowER. Bookkeeper also samples elementary steps substantially faster, adapts to several unseen reaction types with minimal fine-tuning, and generates candidate chemical transformations for further screening. These results suggest that explicit electron bookkeeping is a useful framework for virtually screening chemical reactions across diverse reagents, validating computer-assisted synthesis planning predictions, and providing mechanistic interpretations of reactivity.
